[h2]Wow, what a surprise, I actually prefer this game more than Destiny 2, The Division & Warframe.[/h2]

[u]A F2P player's initial impressions on the game:[/u]
Pros:
+ Combat speed is in the middle of the pack: not as fast as Warframe, not as slow as The Division. It's pretty similar to Destiny 2 in this case. Feels like your character is playing as a Strand guardian with that grappling hook.
+ default Third Person Camera. (this is subjective but still)
+ Decent gunplay. It's not the best, but the hit feeling is good enough not to make me immediately leave the game. It surely has some "oomphs".
+ Beautiful character & world designs.
+ Amazing graphics courtesy of Unreal Engine 5, even on low settings.
+ Story & combat contents are all free. Completely PvE focused as well.
+ The instanced combat contents are scaled just in case you want to do it solo.
+ The main currency and the currency you get to upgrade your mods are easier to farm than Warframe. (You can also auto select duplicate mods to convert which is a huge godsend)
+ Combat difficulty is generally very easy, until the 4th area boss.

Cons:
- No dedicated melee weapons.
- I think the grind here is even heavier than Warframe, which is saying a lot. It's roughly the average Korean MMO levels of grind, minus the 0.000001% enhance chance that plagues the genre.
- Story bores me after a while. I started skipping things after they've shown the dollar store Exo character.
- There's a huge difficulty spike at the 4th area colossi (normal mode). Everyone in The Dead Bride boss fight seems to be very scared of attacking it, making it a huge wall to hurdle. I only managed to break its shield before timing out, when soloing. At this time of writing I decided to grind and increase my power before fighting it again. 
- Shop contents are overpriced.
- The battle pass doesn't refund your spent premium currency as you progress. (Then again, this is Nexon we're talking about, no way they do that)
- You have to run for a bit just to upgrade your mods, and to research something. I wish you can do that on one of the camps, or put them near each other enough.
- The dungeon bosses are VERY spongy if you fight them with a full team and with a levelled unbuilt gear. They pretty much inflate your playtime if you're still progressing.

Overall I'd give this a 6/10. Recommended for those who wanted a third person looter shooter with a more relaxed combat flow, and doesn't mind the heavy grinding.

The First Descendant doesn't fill in the niche of Loot Shooters at all.
First review was a negative experience. After giving it another chance, I honestly enjoy the game.

It's Warframe but worse. It's Destiny but worse. It's [i]ANTHEM[/i] but worse.
If you like endless grind looter shooters with lots of character kits to sink hours into and don't give a thought to any other design elements besides what guns to use and what mods to plug in, you'll like this. If you have anything that keeps you from enjoying noncohesive gameplay systems and the progression therein, and chafe at the prevalence of nondescript PNGs and poorly explained statuses and [b]bolded[/b] verbs and adjectives you need to pay attention to, go elsewhere.

It's flashy and energetic and full of the most overly-designed characters and guns and setpieces that UE5 can render, but without any meaningful substance to back any of it up. Guns [i]sound[/i] meaty but have no feeling for handling, character movements are weightless even with heavier classes, ability use has little meaningful feedback and impact and just sort of occurs, and all the animations for every character are just too much. There comes a point where the big armor pauldron has simply moved around and [b]CLANKED[/b] too much. Sound design overall is alarmingly poor but also overengineered; booms and techno fwooooms are way too loud and frequent to be enjoyed and guns just sound like modern "insert sci-fi weapon type here" stock packs. The only sound that has any serious chop to it is the hitmarker and headshot SFX which are suitably crunchy and satisfying.

Character kits have all the hallmarks of classic archetypes we've been seeing for a decade and there's little in the way of anything new and exciting. The tank makes a big wall and sometimes a dome and sometimes does a big stomp, the damage guy has explosives and fire damage for DoT, the CC lady makes lightning jump around between enemies for big clears, you've seen all of this before. Other characters have more stock kits and very few look to be a worthwhile grind; I wouldn't know, I'm not made of enough money to buy any of these things comfortably. 

When you're actually running around shooting stuff with your team of randoms or friends it can feel like there's something to latch on to. Your abilities are going off, you're shooting the same big boys together and whittling down their health bars, you're clearing groups of enemies with accidental symbiosis, and you can feel that there's something here you can latch on to. You'll pick up your new guns and mods and compare stats that mean nothing but make numbers go higher, so you'll at least feel some sense of your strength as a character getting higher. In these moments, First Descendant may finally feel like a fun time.

And then you'll be ripped out of the experience to talk to the next poorly-voiced NPC who gives you a new quest to go shoot the next Florbo, Scourge of Bungo but only after you watch another overacted cutscene and talk to 4 other NPCs who do nothing but fill out objective markers that are "Talk to Scrungo to upgrade your Bits". You'll have to talk to the one NPC who can make your mods stronger for an increasing fee every time because the idea of you upgrading anything without having to run around the social area is seemingly too much for Nexon. At least that way you can maybe see a player wearing that other character you REALLY want to play with and feel pressured into spending money to get them faster.

You've seen this grind a dozen times by now: get the Small Bit to make the Bigger Bit to make the big newest Toy to play with. Run the same activities over and over and over to collect PNGs that may not be the PNG you need right now, but at least you're collecting stuff! If you're impatient, you can pay money to skip the "research" time so you can use your new Toy sooner. Uh-oh, what's that? The rush payment is just a little too much for just one pack of premium currency? Hope you don't work minimum wage to afford that rush AND the new skin that other player was using that looks REALLY cool. And the premium battle pass, because it's free to play but not free to progress.

It's nothing new, it's the same stuff we've seen time and time again from these kinds of games. It's slop. It's artists turned loose with no oversight and designers answering to overlords trying to make a functioning videogame out of the disparate art assets being turned in. A producer steps into the office to see a demo and leaves 5 minutes in because it runs. An investor is at his own little desk running projections and salivating. If you get enjoyment out of this type of stuff, then you'll be comfortable here. If you're at all tired of modern looter shooters and especially F2P ones at that, you've already skipped this.

The game has excellent shooting mechanics and decent skills. All characters have some useful and at least 1 god awful ability. The story is not really why you play this game. The graphics are beautiful and so are the characters. The voice acting in the English version is not great, but thankfully you can run Korean voices if you want. Trust me, you want to.

It's obvious that the grind here is going to be on par with Warframe or worse. That's not a good thing. 
They really want you to use the in game store to compensate for that, but you don't have to. What I am worried about is the grind getting worse and worse. That would be par for the course from a Korean game, and I have a feeling this game won't be different. 
In addition. Jagged peaks and lots of jagged beautiful scenery is not a good thing in a shooter where you actually have to pay attention to what is happening. Sterile Lands especially is a snag-fest of epic proportions where your character can snag on just about everything. Not fun when trying to get out of a crossfire. 

All in all the total package is worth playing, and even dropping $10-20 USD on the cosmetic MTX if you want to support them. 

Side note: They were not prepared for the interest this game garnered, and the launch has been very rough. Several periods of downtime and lots of weird in game bugs.

Oh and one more thing. That jumping puzzle in the swamp zone? It's god awful and should not be a requirement to progress. Never ever make a jumping puzzle a requirement to progress. Only a few people enjoy them and if you're solo they are a horrible experience. Especially when your grapplehook system doesn't work properly with the plattforms and jumping is a hit-or-miss experience. Who thought this was a good idea?
